blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Most speech large language models (SLMs) still process speech in an offline manner. They only start responding after they receive the complete speech segment. However, many real-world applications require streaming speech interaction, for which the audio continuously flows in and the machine is required to answer questions based on the so far received audio chunks. For example, a user may ask the system to continuously count how many times a person's name has been mentioned while they are speaking. We observe a lack of benchmarks and evaluation protocols for real-time speech interaction. Motivated by this, we propose LibriSpeech-Real-QA, a dataset and a benchmark for real-time speech interaction. We construct different types of real-time question-answer pairs from LibriSpeech to evaluate whether speech LLMs can identify target words in streaming audio. We evaluate several popular real-time commercial models and find that they still tend to respond only after the speech turn has finished. We demonstrate that we can enable a pretrained SLM to perform this task, where we explore several modeling designs and establish a solid baseline for future research.
blocks.zh: 大多数语音大语言模型(SLMS)仍然以离线方式处理语音. 他们只有在收到完整的演讲部分后才开始回应. 然而,许多现实世界的应用需要流体语音交互,为此音频持续流进,机器需要根据迄今为止收到的音频块回答问题. 例如,一个用户可能会要求系统在说话时不断计算一个人的名字被提及的次数. 我们注意到缺乏实时语音互动的基准和评价协议。 为此,我们提议LibriSpeech-Real-QA,一个数据集和一个实时语音互动的基准. 我们从 LibriSpeech 构造了不同类型的实时问答对,以评估语音 LLMS 能否识别流音中的目标单词. 我们评价了几个流行的实时商业模型,发现它们仍然倾向于只在演讲回合结束后才作出反应. 我们表明,我们能够使经过预先培训的可持续土地管理能够完成这项任务,在那里,我们探索若干模型设计,并为今后的研究确定坚实的基线。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
In a human spoken conversation, interlocutors listen to and understand the speech from each other before it is finished. We argue that machines require the same streaming speech interaction capability to better interact with humans in speech.
Speech large language models (SLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities in speech understanding, generation and spoken dialogue [ 1 , 9 , 8 , 24 , 3 ] . However, these models predominantly operate in a strictly turn-based setting, where the complete audio signal needs to be fully available before processing begins.
blocks.zh:
在人语对话中,对话者在演讲结束前听取和理解对方的发言。 我们主张机器需要相同的流体语音互动能力,以便在语音上更好地与人类互动.
语音大语言模型在语音理解、生成和语音对话[1、9、8、24、3]方面表现出了令人印象深刻的能力。 然而,这些模型主要在严格的回合制环境中运行,在开始处理前需要完全提供完整的音频信号.

blocks.en:
Full-duplex spoken interaction [ 2 , 20 , 23 , 6 , 25 , 15 ] is promising to facilitate streaming speech interaction, as it requires models to automatically decide their dialogue state in real-time, i.e., to continue listening, continue speaking, convert from listen to speak or vice versa.
However, the typical evaluation scenarios are turn-taking, user interruption and backchannels [ 13 , 12 ] , and there is a lack of explicit evaluation regarding fine-grained streaming speech interaction capabilities, such as quick assistant responses during streaming speech.
blocks.zh:
完全繁复的语音互动[2,20,23,6,25,15]有望促进流畅的语音互动,因为它需要模型在实时中自动决定其对话状态,即继续聆听,继续演讲,从听到说话转换或者反之.
然而,典型的评价设想是转弯,用户中断和回路[13,12],对精细的流线语音交互能力缺乏明确的评价,例如在流线语音中快速的助手响应.

blocks.en: More recently, speech interactions have evolved beyond the full-duplex spoken dialogue towards more general real-time speech and audio interaction. Audio Interaction model [ 21 ] proposes Proactive-Sound-Bench to evaluate a series of audio-event-triggered proactive response tasks. Thinking Machines Lab reports an interesting internal evaluation task for their Interaction Models [ 10 ] to identify certain words in an audio stream in real-time. We believe that such curated streaming speech interaction tasks can serve as an important indicator for the SLM in terms of their streaming speech processing and real-time interaction capabilities, but we have not seen open benchmarks regarding these capabilities.
blocks.zh: 最近,语音互动已经超越了完全繁复的语音对话,转向了更普遍的实时语音和音频互动. Audio Interactive model [21] 提出主动-声奔驰,评价一系列音频-事件触发的主动响应任务. Think Machines Lab报告了一个有趣的内部评价任务,用于他们的交互模型[10]实时识别音频流中的某些单词. 我们认为,这种经过整理的流派语音互动任务能够成为可持续土地管理在流派语音处理和实时互动能力方面的一个重要指标,但我们尚未看到关于这些能力的公开基准。

blocks.en: Traditional streaming speech processing tasks, such as streaming speech recognition [ 7 ] and translation [ 11 ] , can also serve as proxy tasks for streaming speech interaction. However, they emphasize more on the passive processing of the speech signal, leaving proactive interaction capabilities of the SLMs untested.
blocks.zh: 传统的流传语音处理任务,如流传语音识别[7]和翻译[11],也可以作为流传语音交互的代理任务. 然而,它们更强调被动处理语音信号,使可持续土地管理的积极互动能力得不到检验。

blocks.en: To address these gaps, we introduce LibriSpeech-Real-QA , a benchmark for streaming speech interaction and question answering constructed from LibriSpeech [ 18 ] corpus. The benchmark covers four types of tasks that follow the same format: the model receives a speech stream together with a prompt that asks it to emit an answer when the queried event is heard. The types cross a lexical or semantic target with detection or counting (Section 2.1 ). They allow us to evaluate real-time speech understanding, instruction following, and proactive response generation. We propose a corresponding metric calculation protocol to evaluate streaming SLMs’ predictions with emission-level recall, precision, F1-score, and onset delay. Finally, we present a finetuning approach for adapting a pretrained SLM—Qwen2.5-Omni [ 22 ] —to our proposed streaming speech interaction tasks, establishing strong baselines for future research.
blocks.zh: 为了弥补这些差距,我们引入了LibriSpeech-Real-QA,这是LibriSpeech [18] acident构建的流媒体语音互动和问答的基准. 该基准包括了四类遵循相同格式的任务:模型收到一个语音流,以及一个请其在听到被询问事件时发出答案的提示. 这些类型通过检测或计数跨越词汇或语义目标(第2.1节)。 它们使我们能够评估实时的语音理解、后续指示和积极主动的反应。 我们提出相应的计量计算协议,以排放水平回溯、精确度、F1分数和触发延迟来评估流流中的可持续土地管理预测。 最后,我们提出一种微调办法,以调整经过预先培训的SLMXWEN2.5-Omni[22]——以适应我们提议的流派语音互动任务,为今后的研究确定强有力的基线。

blocks.en: 2 Benchmark Design
blocks.zh: 2 基准设计

blocks.en: 2.1 Task Definitions
blocks.zh: 2.1 任务定义

blocks.en: We define four streaming question answering tasks. In each task, a model receives an audio stream along with a natural language prompt and must output natural language tokens at appropriate times.
blocks.zh: 我们定义了四个串流问题回答任务。 在每项任务中,一个模型会收到一个音频流,同时有一个自然语言的提示,并且必须在适当的时间输出自然语言的符号.

blocks.en: • Lexical Detection. Given a target word w w , the model must output w w immediately each time it hears w w in the audio stream. • Lexical Counting. Given a target word w w , the model maintains a running count and outputs the updated count immediately after each occurrence of w w . • Semantic Detection. Given a semantic class c c (e.g., “animal,” “city”), the model must output each word as soon as it hears a word belonging to class c c . • Semantic Counting. Given a semantic class c c , the model maintains a running count and outputs the updated count whenever a word belonging to c c is heard.
blocks.zh: • 特征检测。 鉴于一个目标词w w ,该模型每次在音频流中听到w w 时必须立刻输出w w. • 统计。 鉴于目标词w w ,该模型维持一个运行中的计数,并在w w 的每次发生后立即输出更新的计数. ^ 语义检测. 鉴于一个语义类c c(如"动物","城市"),模型在听到一个属于类c的词时,必须立即输出每个词. ^ 语义计数. 鉴于一个语义类c c ,该模型维持一个运行中的计数,每当听到属于 c c 的单词时都会输出更新的计数.

blocks.zh: 光谱探测器 鉴于一个目标词w w ,该模型每次在音频流中听到w w 时必须立刻输出w w.

blocks.en: Lexical Counting. Given a target word w w , the model maintains a running count and outputs the updated count immediately after each occurrence of w w .
blocks.zh: 历法计数. 鉴于一个目标词w w ,该模型维持一个运行中的计数,并在w w每次发生后立即输出更新的计数.

blocks.en: Semantic Detection. Given a semantic class c c (e.g., “animal,” “city”), the model must output each word as soon as it hears a word belonging to class c c .
blocks.zh: 语义侦测. 鉴于一个语义类c c(如“动物”,”“城市”),模型一听到属于c类的单词,就必须立即输出每个单词。

blocks.en: Semantic Counting. Given a semantic class c c , the model maintains a running count and outputs the updated count whenever a word belonging to c c is heard.
blocks.zh: 语义计数. 鉴于一个语义类c c ,该模型维持一个运行中的计数,每当听到属于 c c 的单词时都会输出更新的计数.

blocks.en: 2.2 Data Construction
blocks.zh: 2.2 国家 数据构建

blocks.en: We construct a dataset for the proposed tasks from the LibriSpeech corpus [ 18 ] . As shown in Table 1 , it follows the LibriSpeech partition: a training set constructed from train-clean-100 , train-clean-360 , and train-other-500 ; a development set from dev-clean and dev-other ; and a benchmark from test-clean and test-other . Each utterance is annotated with three domains: the system prompt, the list of target words, and their timestamps. The annotations are produced by a pipeline of four stages as described below.
blocks.zh: 我们为LibriSpeech程序书的拟议任务构建了一个数据集。 如表1所示,它遵循LibriSpeech分区:由列车-清洁-100型、列车-清洁-360型和列车-其他-500型建造的一套培训;由dev-clean型和dev-other型开发的一套培训;以及由测试-清洁型和测试-其他型建设的基准。 每句话都附加三个领域:系统提示,目标单词列表,及其时间戳. 说明由以下四个阶段的管道编写。

blocks.en: Stage 1: Forced Alignment. We obtain word-level timestamps using a force-aligner such as Montreal Forced Aligner (MFA) alignments [ 16 ] . Each word is assigned a start time and end time.
blocks.zh: 第一阶段:强制调整。 我们使用诸如蒙特利尔强制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制的调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制调制 [16] 每个单词都被指定一个开始时间和结束时间.

blocks.en: Stage 2: Semantic Classification. We classify words into one of 20 semantic categories (including person_name , animal , city , profession , organization , food , plant , color , body_part , cardinal , ordinal , kinship , date , clock_time , country , money , disease , weather , state_or_province and Null ) using an LLM with a structured extraction prompt. Classified semantic labels are stored alongside timestamps in the metadata.
blocks.zh: 阶段2:语义分类. 我们把词分为20个语义类之一(包括人物_名称,动物,城市,职业,组织,食物,植物,颜色,身体_部位,红衣,正统,亲缘关系,日期,钟表_时间,国家,金钱,疾病,天气,状态_或_省及Null),使用有结构的提取提示的LLM. 分类语义标签与时间戳一起存储在元数据中.

blocks.en: Stage 3: Sample Generation. For each utterance, we select target words and semantic classes that appear in the metadata, and we fill a prompt template with the chosen target. The prompt is the instruction for one of the four tasks in Section 2.1 . A lexical-detection example is: “The moment you hear the word ‘warriors’ in the stream, say it out loud.” When a target occurs more than once, we keep the sample only if consecutive occurrences are separated by more than one second, leaving the downstream model ample time to emit an answer before the next event. Lexical and semantic counting samples are built only when the target occurs multiple times.
blocks.zh: 第3阶段:样本生成。 对于每句话,我们都会选择元数据中出现的目标词和语义类,我们用选定的目标填充一个即时模板. 第2.1节中的四项任务之一的指示是提示。 一个词典检测的例子是 : “ 你听到溪流中的‘警告者'一词的时候,大声说出来。 ” 当一个目标不止一次发生时,我们只保留当连续发生的时间间隔超过一秒时的样本,让下游模型有足够的时间在下一次事件之前发出答案. 只有当目标发生多次时,才会建立表征和语义计数样本.

blocks.en: Stage 4: Negative Sample Generation. The samples from Stage 3 are positive: the utterance always contains the word or semantic class named in the prompt. We also build negative samples, in which that target is absent, so the correct behavior for the model is to remain silent. Without exposing to negative samples, a model can treat every utterance as one that requires an answer while including them in training reduces that bias.
blocks.zh: 阶段4:负样本生成. 来自第3阶段的样本为阳性: 语句中总是包含在提示中命名的单词或语义类. 我们还建立了负面的样本,其中没有这个目标,所以模型的正确行为就是保持沉默. 在不暴露于负面样品的情况下,一个模型可以将每句话当作一个需要回答的话,同时将它们纳入培训会减少这种偏见。

blocks.en: 2.3 Evaluation Protocol
blocks.zh: 2.3 评价议定书

blocks.en: The benchmark evaluates models that take streaming speech input chunk by chunk, with chunk duration C C , and emit a response as soon as the queried target is heard. Both the time and the content of the response are scored in the evaluation.
blocks.zh: 该基准评价了逐块进行流式语音输入的模型,其时间跨度为C,一旦听到被询问的目标,即发出答复。 回应的时间和内容均在评价中得分.

blocks.en:
Each occurrence of the target word is a reference event. For detection the target content is the word text, and for counting it is the updated count at that word. The event occupies the aligned interval [ t start , t end ] [t_{\mathrm{start}},t_{\mathrm{end}}] in the streaming speech.
For each event, we define its acceptance window as [ t start , t end + g ] [t_{\mathrm{start}},\,t_{\mathrm{end}}+g] . It opens when the word starts and remains open for a grace period g g after the word ends in the stream speech.
A model emission is considered as a hit only when its onset ( t ^ \hat{t} ) is within the acceptance window of the event and its content agrees with the event and the prompt.

目标词的每个发生都是参考事件. 为了检测目标内容是文字一词,为了计算,它是该词的更新数. 该事件占用了串流语句中的对齐间隔 [t start, t end] [t_{\mathrm{start}}, t_{\mathrm{end}}].
对于每个事件,我们将其接受窗口定义为 [t start, t end + g] [t_{\mathrm{ start}},\, t_{\mathrm{end}}+g]. 它在单词开始时打开,并在单词结束于溪流语音后保持宽限期g.
模型排放只有在其发生(t ^\ hat{t})在事件的接受窗口内且其内容与事件和即时一致时才被视为命中.

blocks.en: We use N ref N_{\mathrm{ref}} to denote the number of reference events and TP \mathrm{TP} for the number of hits. A miss is a reference event that receives no hit, so the number of misses is N ref − TP N_{\mathrm{ref}}-\mathrm{TP} . A false alarm ( FA \mathrm{FA} ) is a model emission that matches no event.

We report fuzzy matching, under which the reference text only needs to occur inside the prediction. Exact matching requires the two normalized strings to be identical.

We also calculate the mean onset delay d ¯ \overline{d} which averages t ^ − t start \hat{t}-t_{\mathrm{start}} over hits. Counting uses the same matching rule, with each count update as its own event, so both the count and the onset must be correct.

blocks.en: 3 Streaming Model Baseline
blocks.zh: 3 流式模型基线

blocks.en: We adapt Qwen2.5-Omni-7B [ 22 ] to perform the proposed tasks by a sequence of causal decisions at chunk boundaries: after each fixed-duration chunk the model either stays silent (by emitting a special silence token) or emits the target content once the queried event becomes observable.
blocks.zh: 我们调整了Quen2.5-Omni-7B[22],以便在块边界上通过一系列因果决定来完成拟议任务:在每次固定期限块之后,模型要么保持沉默(发出特别的沉默令牌),要么在被询问事件被观察到后发出目标内容。

blocks.en: 3.1 Modeling Formulation
blocks.zh: 3.1 制作模型

blocks.en: We divide an audio stream into K K consecutive chunks x 1 , … , x K x_{1},\ldots,x_{K} each lasting C C seconds, represented in the native multi-turn format of Qwen2.5-Omni as [ system ] , { [ user ⁡ ( x k ) , assistant ⁡ ( y k ) ] } k = 1 K [\mathrm{system}],\{[\mathrm{user}(x_{k}),\mathrm{assistant}(y_{k})]\}_{k=1}^{K} . Each user turn contains only the newly arrived chunk, so predicting y k y_{k} accesses only the causal prefix x 1 , … , x k x_{1},\ldots,x_{k} .

At each chunk boundary, the model implicitly selects one of two actions: SPEAK or SILENCE . A SPEAK decision emits a meaningful content, followed by the end-of-turn token <|im_end|> , whereas a SILENCE decision emits the
special token <keep_silence> followed by <|im_end|> . We also utilize negative samples as described in Sec 2.2 during training. It teaches the model to remain silent when the audio stream does not contain the queried target.
We freeze the audio encoder and disable the speech-generation talker branch. blocks.en: 4.2 Baseline Results
blocks.zh: 4.2 基线结果

blocks.en: Tables 2 – 5 report results on the four tasks for the test-clean and test-other splits. Existing real-time speech APIs can identify some queried events, particularly in lexical detection, but do not exhibit the event-triggered response behavior required by our tasks. Their mean onset delays are several seconds, consistent with treating the input as a conversational turn and responding near the end of the utterance rather than when the queried event occurs. These delays are not a controlled latency comparison across providers, as they also reflect differences in response policies and service conditions. Instead, the results demonstrate the value of LibriSpeech-Real-QA: by evaluating both what a model emits and when it emits it, the benchmark reveals a gap in fine-grained streaming speech interaction that content-only or turn-level evaluation would miss.
blocks.zh: 表2 – 5 报告测试清洁和测试其他拆分的四个任务的结果. 现有的实时语音API可以识别一些被询问的事件,特别是在词汇检测中,但不显示我们的任务所要求的事件触发反应行为. 它们的平均触发延迟是几秒钟,这与把输入作为对话的转折,在言论结束时而不是在被询问的事件发生时作出反应相一致。 这些拖延并不是各供应商之间可控的延迟比较,因为它们也反映了反应政策和服务条件的差异。 相反,这些结果显示了LibriSpeech-Real-QA的价值:通过评价一个模型的什么发出以及当它发出时,该基准揭示了精细的流线语音交互上的一个空白,即只内容或回合级的评价会错过.

blocks.en: 4.3 Streaming Finetuning Results
blocks.zh: 4.3 精简结果

blocks.en:
Overall comparison. Streaming finetuning enables Qwen2.5-Omni-7B to respond during the
speech stream and improves F1 over the pretrained model on every task
and split. It also outperforms the evaluated real-time APIs in F1
across all four tasks. Under the +1c window, the 400 400 ms
streaming model achieves 0.988 / 0.968 0.988/0.968 F1 on lexical detection and 0.824 / 0.694 0.824/0.694 on semantic detection, exceeding the corresponding Offline results while making causal decisions. In contrast, Offline remains stronger on both counting tasks. These
results establish a strong causal baseline and show why the
benchmark must evaluate response timing alongside answer content.

语音流和改进 F1 相对于每个任务的预训模型
并分开。 也比F1的实时API好
所有四项任务。 在+1c窗口下,400 400 ms
流线模型实现0.988/0.968 0.988/0.968 F1 (b) 超过相应的离线结果,同时作出因果关系决定。 相比之下,离线在两项计数任务上仍然更强大。 这些
结果确定了一个强有力的因果关系基线,并表明为什么
基准必须评价答复时间和答复内容。

blocks.en:
Task-wise comparison. For our finetuned Streaming model, the semantic tasks generally yield lower F1 than the corresponding lexical tasks, indicating that they are more challenging in this setting. This is expected because semantic tasks require the model to relate the speech signal to the meaning of the queried class, whereas lexical tasks require it to recognize a specified word.
Comparing detection and counting reveals different patterns across the two task families. For lexical tasks, counting is more challenging than detection; for the finetuned streaming models, semantic detection has lower F1 than semantic counting.
For lexical tasks, detecting a repeated target word is sufficient for detection, but counting also requires the model to maintain and update a cumulative count after each occurrence. For semantic tasks, both tasks require recognizing class membership, but detection must additionally identify and output the particular word heard at each event; counting only needs to output the updated count.
blocks.zh:
任务比较。 对于我们微调的Streaming模型来说,语义任务一般产生比相应的Lexical任务更低的F1,表明它们在这个背景下更具挑战性. 这是因为语义任务需要模型将语音信号与被询问类的含义联系起来,而语法任务则需要它识别一个指定的单词.
比较检测和计数揭示了两个任务家庭的不同模式。 对于词汇任务,计数比检测更具挑战性;对于微调的流线模型,语义检测的F1比语义计数要低.
对于词汇任务,检测一个重复的目标词就足以检测,但计数还需要模型在每次发生后维持和更新一个累积计数. 对于语义任务,两个任务都需要识别类成员,但检测必须额外识别并输出每个事件听到的特定单词;计数只需要输出更新的计数.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We introduced LibriSpeech-Real-QA, a benchmark for event-triggered
streaming speech interaction. Its temporal evaluation protocol
assesses both the content and timing of model responses, revealing
that existing real-time speech APIs often respond near the end of an
utterance rather than when a queried event occurs. We also showed
that streaming finetuning can adapt a pretrained SLM to make causal,
event-level responses, establishing baselines across chunk durations
and exposing task-dependent accuracy–delay trade-offs. The benchmark
provides a basis for developing speech models that answer while
speech is still unfolding.
blocks.zh:
我们介绍了LibriSpeech-Real-QA,这是事件触发的基准
流媒体语音互动。 其时间评估协议
评估模型反应的内容和时间,揭示
现有的实时语音 API 经常在接近一个
而不是当被询问的事件发生时 我们还展示了
流体微调可以调整预先经过训练的可持续土地管理,以产生因果关系,
事件层面的应对措施,确定跨块长度的基线
并暴露了任务依赖的准确性-延迟权衡。 基准
提供基础,以开发在回答的同时
演讲还在展开。
